Review result: no blockers. P3 issue #2718, effort:high; one collaborator review is enough for the merge rule.

What we checked. We merged the head into current main in a review worktree; the merge is clean (#2664 is on main, so this PR refines the code that shipped). We built and tested that tree, debug: `camcraft-app` lib 384 pass, 0 fail (the four new lattice pins run there); the seven import suites green (6+1+26+2+4+6+3), `tilted_gouge` full-fidelity pin holds with the bar at 0.005 mm; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The STEP import time did not grow out of hand (fixture batch 15.1 s).

Law check. The report is now honest in the right direction. The kept facets' highest edge (inside and boundary) times the kind's inside bound is what the import reports; a boundary edge is measured but never split, so the shell stays closed and a coarse boundary shows up as reduced fidelity, not as a silent pass. The inside bound is 4/3 from the simplex-interpolation result (Waldron 1998, public literature) with a margin at 1.5; the cylinder's 1.0 argument is right: the deviation depends on the curved parameter only, so its extreme lies on an edge. Each pin asserts both sides (reported not below the sampled worst, not above twice it), so a future kind that breaks the bound fails visibly. A non-finite measure becomes `INFINITY`, which fails the import rather than passing it. Splitting inside edges to `tol / inside()` makes the split limit match the report; the old pair (split at 2 x tol, report tol) is what caused #2718.

Notes, not blockers. Finer inside splits cost facets on cone-like faces that run to a budget break; the kept (coarser) edges are then measured and reported, so the cost shows as a refusal, never as a wrong pass. `feature_edge_g1_join` (#2713) is red on main for the same fixture family; this PR neither fixes nor worsens it, and #2731 is correctly not claimed to close it.

Verdict: ready to merge when flagged ready. Label set to merge-ready.

Merge class: SAME. The head is `c8afe25f647a9990bbce77af3f8bc4f01aeeaca7`, the head that the review names (comment 7004009337). No commit came after that review. The PR merges cleanly with `main`. This merge relies on that review. The PR fixes a P3 issue, so one collaborator review is sufficient. PR #2732 is stacked on this PR and its base is already `main`.
